@graph.articleBody: Knowledge distillation is not one technique but a family of at least two dozen distinct methods, separated by what signal crosses from teacher to student (logits, hidden features, pairwise relations, sampled text, preferences, or denoising trajectories) and by whether you can open the teacher at all. This library catalogues 27 methods with their loss functions, data and access requirements, tooling, and honest trade-offs. The central split is white-box versus black-box: white-box methods (soft targets, feature hints, reverse-KL, on-policy GKD) need teacher logits or activations and give the densest supervision per token, while black-box methods (SFT on API outputs, chain-of-thought and reasoning-trace distillation) need only sampled text and are what most practitioners actually run — and what triggered the 2025-2026 legal fights. The frontier has moved from static logit matching to on-policy methods where the student generates and the teacher grades: the Qwen3 technical report (Table 21) gives 74.4% on AIME'24 for a Qwen3-8B student at 1,800 GPU-hours of on-policy distillation versus 67.6% for RL at 17,920 GPU-hours, and Thinking Machines reproduced the method on the Tinker API. Method choice is mostly determined by three constraints — teacher access, label availability, and whether the student's architecture or tokenizer matches the teacher's — and this library is organised so you can walk those three constraints to a shortlist.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Knowledge distillation (KD)
hasDefinedTerm.description: Training a student model to reproduce the behaviour of a teacher model, using the teacher's outputs, internal states or generated data as the supervision signal instead of (or alongside) ground-truth labels.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Teacher
hasDefinedTerm.description: The model whose behaviour is being copied. Usually larger, slower or more expensive than the student; occasionally the same size (self-distillation) or even a peer (mutual learning).

hasDefinedTerm.name: Student
hasDefinedTerm.description: The model being trained. Its capacity ceiling, not the loss function, is usually what limits how much of the teacher survives the transfer.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Soft targets
hasDefinedTerm.description: The teacher's full probability distribution over classes or tokens, as opposed to a one-hot label. Carries information about which wrong answers were nearly right.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Dark knowledge
hasDefinedTerm.description: Hinton's informal name for the information in the relative probabilities the teacher assigns to incorrect classes — the part of the teacher's judgement that a hard label throws away.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Temperature (T)
hasDefinedTerm.description: A divisor applied to logits before the softmax. Higher T flattens the distribution and exposes small probability differences. Because gradients through the softened softmax scale as 1/T^2, the soft-target loss term is multiplied by T^2.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Forward KL
hasDefinedTerm.description: KL(teacher || student). Mass-covering: it punishes the student for assigning low probability anywhere the teacher assigns mass, so an under-capacity student smears probability across modes it cannot represent.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Reverse KL
hasDefinedTerm.description: KL(student || teacher). Mode-seeking: it punishes the student only where the student itself puts mass, so a small student concentrates on the teacher's dominant modes instead of hedging. The core of MiniLLM.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Generalized JSD
hasDefinedTerm.description: A beta-interpolated Jensen-Shannon divergence used in GKD. Beta = 0 approximates forward KL, beta = 1 approximates reverse KL, and intermediate values trade off between them.

hasDefinedTerm.name: On-policy distillation
hasDefinedTerm.description: Sampling training sequences from the student and having the teacher score them token by token, so the student is corrected exactly on the distribution it will actually produce at inference.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Off-policy distillation
hasDefinedTerm.description: Training on a fixed corpus of teacher-generated (or human) sequences. Simpler and cheaper, but the student never sees its own mistakes during training.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Exposure bias
hasDefinedTerm.description: The compounding error that occurs when an autoregressive model trained only on teacher-forced sequences meets its own generated prefixes at inference. The problem on-policy distillation exists to solve.

hasDefinedTerm.name: White-box distillation
hasDefinedTerm.description: Distillation that requires access to teacher internals — logits, hidden states, attention maps or gradients. Only possible when you can run the teacher's weights yourself.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Black-box distillation
hasDefinedTerm.description: Distillation from sampled teacher outputs only, as returned by an API. The dominant mode in practice, and the mode governed by API terms of service.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Sequence-level KD
hasDefinedTerm.description: Replacing token-level distribution matching with plain maximum-likelihood training on complete sequences generated by the teacher, typically its beam-search output.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Rationale distillation
hasDefinedTerm.description: Training the student to reproduce the teacher's reasoning text as an auxiliary target, not just its final answer. Distilling Step-by-Step frames this as a second task in a multi-task objective.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Reasoning-trace distillation
hasDefinedTerm.description: Supervised fine-tuning on long chain-of-thought traces from a reasoning teacher, as in the DeepSeek-R1-Distill family (800k samples) and s1 (1,000 samples). No RL stage is required.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Budget forcing
hasDefinedTerm.description: An inference-time control from s1 that either cuts off a model's thinking or extends it by appending 'Wait', trading test-time compute for accuracy on a model already distilled on reasoning traces.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Capacity gap
hasDefinedTerm.description: The empirical finding that distillation degrades when teacher and student are too far apart in size, motivating teacher-assistant chains and mode-seeking divergences.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Teacher correction
hasDefinedTerm.description: Lightly fine-tuning the teacher on the distillation corpus before distilling, so the teacher's distribution matches the transfer data. Named by NVIDIA in the Minitron work and independently confirmed in the torchtune case study.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Hint layer
hasDefinedTerm.description: The teacher's intermediate layer chosen as a feature-matching target in FitNets, paired with a learned regressor that maps the narrower student layer into the teacher's dimensionality.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Attention map
hasDefinedTerm.description: A spatial energy map derived by summing the absolute powers of a layer's channel activations. Attention transfer matches L2-normalised versions of these between teacher and student.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Relation-based knowledge
hasDefinedTerm.description: Structure that lives between examples rather than within one — pairwise distances and triplet angles in embedding space. What RKD transfers.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Cross-tokenizer distillation
hasDefinedTerm.description: Distilling between models with different vocabularies. Requires either an optimal-transport cost over sorted probabilities (ULD) or a shared projected output space with cross-model attention (DSKD).

hasDefinedTerm.name: Dataset distillation
hasDefinedTerm.description: Compressing a training set into a small synthetic set that trains a model to comparable accuracy, via bi-level optimisation. The model is fixed; the data is the thing being distilled.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Preference distillation
hasDefinedTerm.description: Using a teacher (or an AI judge) to rank candidate completions and training the student on those preferences, via a reward model plus RL (RLAIF) or directly (dDPO).

hasDefinedTerm.name: Speculative decoding
hasDefinedTerm.description: An exact-inference speedup where a cheap draft model proposes several tokens and the target model verifies them in one pass. Distillation enters as the method for training draft heads (EAGLE, Medusa) that get accepted more often.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Progressive distillation
hasDefinedTerm.description: Repeatedly halving a diffusion sampler's step count by training a student to take in one step what the teacher takes in two, compounding to large speedups over several rounds.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Consistency model
hasDefinedTerm.description: A generative model trained so that all points on a probability-flow ODE trajectory map to the same origin, permitting one-step sampling. Can be distilled from a diffusion teacher or trained standalone.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Context distillation
hasDefinedTerm.description: Compiling a prompt — instructions, few-shot examples or scratchpad reasoning — into model weights by training the model without the context to match its own predictions with the context.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Distillation attack
hasDefinedTerm.description: Anthropic's term for coordinated, large-scale extraction of a hosted model's outputs across fraudulent accounts in order to train a competing model, as distinct from a legitimate managed distillation workflow.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Response-based KD (soft targets with temperature)
hasDefinedTerm.description: The founding method. Train the student to match the teacher's temperature-softened output distribution, optionally blended with ordinary cross-entropy against ground-truth labels.

subjectOf.name: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network

hasDefinedTerm.name: Feature / intermediate-layer KD (FitNets hints)
hasDefinedTerm.description: Supervise a student's hidden layer directly against a teacher's hidden layer, using a learned projector to bridge the width mismatch, then finish with ordinary response-based KD.

subjectOf.name: FitNets: Hints for Thin Deep Nets

hasDefinedTerm.name: Attention transfer
hasDefinedTerm.description: Instead of matching full activation tensors, match a cheap 2-D summary of where each layer is 'looking' — the channel-collapsed activation energy map — after L2 normalisation.

subjectOf.name: Paying More Attention to Attention: Improving the Performance of Convolutional Neural Networks via Attention Transfer

hasDefinedTerm.name: Relational KD (RKD)
hasDefinedTerm.description: Transfer the geometry *between* examples — pairwise distances and triplet angles in embedding space — rather than the representation of any single example.

subjectOf.name: Relational Knowledge Distillation

hasDefinedTerm.name: Contrastive representation distillation (CRD)
hasDefinedTerm.description: Reframe distillation as maximising the mutual information between teacher and student representations, optimised with a contrastive (InfoNCE-style) objective over positive and negative pairs.

subjectOf.name: Contrastive Representation Distillation

hasDefinedTerm.name: Transformer-layer KD (TinyBERT / DistilBERT)
hasDefinedTerm.description: The standard recipe for compressing encoder transformers: simultaneously match embeddings, attention matrices, hidden states and prediction logits, applied at both the pretraining and task-specific stages.

subjectOf.name: TinyBERT: Distilling BERT for Natural Language Understanding

hasDefinedTerm.name: Sequence-level KD (Kim & Rush)
hasDefinedTerm.description: Replace token-level distribution matching with plain maximum-likelihood training on complete sequences generated by the teacher, typically its beam-search output.

subjectOf.name: Sequence-Level Knowledge Distillation

hasDefinedTerm.name: Black-box output distillation (Alpaca / Vicuna / Orca style)
hasDefinedTerm.description: Generate a synthetic instruction-following dataset by prompting a strong API teacher, then supervised-fine-tune an open base model on it. The dominant form of distillation actually practised.

subjectOf.name: Alpaca: A Strong, Replicable Instruction-Following Model; Orca: Progressive Learning from Complex Explanation Traces of GPT-4

hasDefinedTerm.name: Chain-of-thought / rationale distillation
hasDefinedTerm.description: Extract the teacher's reasoning text as a second supervised target alongside the label, training the student in a multi-task framework to produce both the rationale and the answer.

subjectOf.name: Distilling Step-by-Step! Outperforming Larger Language Models with Less Training Data and Smaller Model Sizes

hasDefinedTerm.name: Reasoning-trace distillation (DeepSeek-R1-Distill, s1)
hasDefinedTerm.description: Supervised fine-tuning on long chain-of-thought traces from a dedicated reasoning teacher, with no reinforcement-learning stage. The single most-copied recipe of 2025.

subjectOf.name: DeepSeek-R1 (Nature, 2025); s1: Simple test-time scaling

hasDefinedTerm.name: Reverse-KL distillation (MiniLLM)
hasDefinedTerm.description: Swap forward KL for reverse KL so the student concentrates on the teacher's dominant modes instead of smearing probability over regions it cannot represent, optimised on the student's own samples.

subjectOf.name: MiniLLM: On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models

hasDefinedTerm.name: Generalized KD (GKD, on-policy)
hasDefinedTerm.description: Train the student on its own generated sequences with teacher feedback on each token, using a beta-interpolated Jensen-Shannon divergence so you can dial continuously between forward and reverse KL.

subjectOf.name: On-Policy Distillation of Language Models: Learning from Self-Generated Mistakes

hasDefinedTerm.name: Speculative knowledge distillation (SKD)
hasDefinedTerm.description: The student proposes tokens and the teacher replaces the poorly ranked ones, producing training sequences that stay near the student's distribution while remaining high quality.

subjectOf.name: Speculative Knowledge Distillation: Bridging the Teacher-Student Gap Through Interleaved Sampling

hasDefinedTerm.name: Self-distillation (Born-Again Networks)
hasDefinedTerm.description: Distil a trained model into a student with an identical architecture and parameter count. The student reliably beats the teacher, and repeating the process compounds the gain.

subjectOf.name: Born Again Neural Networks

hasDefinedTerm.name: Teacher-assistant KD (TAKD)
hasDefinedTerm.description: Insert one or more intermediate-sized models between a very large teacher and a very small student, distilling in a chain, to fix the capacity-gap failure.

subjectOf.name: Improved Knowledge Distillation via Teacher Assistant: Bridging the Gap Between Student and Teacher

hasDefinedTerm.name: Multi-teacher KD
hasDefinedTerm.description: Distil from several teachers at once, combining their output distributions (or features) into a single target for the student.

subjectOf.name: Efficient Knowledge Distillation from an Ensemble of Teachers (Fukuda et al., Interspeech 2017); weighting variants surveyed in Knowledge Distillation: A Survey (Gou et al., 2020, arXiv 2006.05525)

hasDefinedTerm.name: Deep mutual learning (online distillation)
hasDefinedTerm.description: Train a cohort of untrained peer networks simultaneously, each learning from the labels and from the others' predictions. No pretrained teacher exists at any point — every peer is white-box to every other.

subjectOf.name: Deep Mutual Learning

hasDefinedTerm.name: Pruning + distillation (Minitron, Sheared LLaMA)
hasDefinedTerm.description: Structurally prune a large model down to a target shape, then use distillation from the unpruned original to recover the lost accuracy on a small fraction of the original token budget.

subjectOf.name: Compact Language Models via Pruning and Knowledge Distillation; LLM Pruning and Distillation in Practice: The Minitron Approach; Sheared LLaMA

hasDefinedTerm.name: Quantization-aware distillation (QAD / LLM-QAT)
hasDefinedTerm.description: Train a low-bit student with quantization simulated in the loop while distilling from the full-precision original, recovering the accuracy that post-training quantization loses.

subjectOf.name: LLM-QAT: Data-Free Quantization Aware Training for Large Language Models

hasDefinedTerm.name: Dataset distillation / condensation
hasDefinedTerm.description: Hold the model fixed and compress the *training set* into a tiny synthetic set that trains a network to comparable accuracy. The data, not the network, is the thing distilled.

subjectOf.name: Dataset Distillation

hasDefinedTerm.name: Preference distillation / RLAIF
hasDefinedTerm.description: Distil judgement rather than answers: a teacher model ranks candidate completions, those rankings train a reward model, and the student is optimised against it — human annotation replaced by AI feedback.

subjectOf.name: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback; Zephyr: Direct Distillation of LM Alignment

hasDefinedTerm.name: DPO on teacher preferences (dDPO)
hasDefinedTerm.description: Skip the reward model and the RL loop: optimise the student directly on teacher-ranked preference pairs with a simple classification-style loss.

subjectOf.name: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model; Zephyr: Direct Distillation of LM Alignment

hasDefinedTerm.name: Cross-vocabulary logit KD (ULD, DSKD)
hasDefinedTerm.description: Make white-box logit distillation work when teacher and student have different tokenizers, either by comparing sorted probability vectors with an optimal-transport cost or by projecting both models into a shared output space.

subjectOf.name: Towards Cross-Tokenizer Distillation: the Universal Logit Distillation Loss for LLMs; Dual-Space Knowledge Distillation for Large Language Models

hasDefinedTerm.name: Draft-model distillation for speculative decoding (EAGLE, Medusa)
hasDefinedTerm.description: Distil a tiny draft head from a frozen target model so that speculative decoding accepts more proposed tokens. The target model's output distribution is provably unchanged; only latency falls.

subjectOf.name: EAGLE: Speculative Sampling Requires Rethinking Feature Uncertainty; Medusa: Simple LLM Inference Acceleration Framework with Multiple Decoding Heads

hasDefinedTerm.name: Retriever distillation (cross-encoder into bi-encoder)
hasDefinedTerm.description: Distil a slow, accurate cross-encoder ranker into a fast bi-encoder or late-interaction model by matching relevance-score margins, making high-quality dense retrieval affordable at web scale.

subjectOf.name: Improving Efficient Neural Ranking Models with Cross-Architecture Knowledge Distillation (Margin-MSE)

hasDefinedTerm.name: Diffusion distillation (progressive, consistency, LCM, adversarial)
hasDefinedTerm.description: Compress the number of sampling steps rather than the parameter count: train a student to jump along the denoising trajectory in one step where the teacher took many.

subjectOf.name: Progressive Distillation for Fast Sampling of Diffusion Models; Consistency Models; Latent Consistency Models; Adversarial Diffusion Distillation

hasDefinedTerm.name: Context / prompt distillation
hasDefinedTerm.description: Compile a prompt into the weights: train the model without the context to match the predictions of the same model given the context, so instructions, examples and scratchpad reasoning become behaviour.

subjectOf.name: A General Language Assistant as a Laboratory for Alignment (Askell et al.); Learning by Distilling Context (Snell, Klein & Zhong)
